en: Among women who take delight in men, who possess manifold minds and are unrestrained;
“If she should not be pleasing in every respect,
one should not trust her, for women are like a riverbank.
Having seen what [happened] to Kaṇḍarī and the Kinnaras...”
No women find delight in the household life;
having abandoned such a husband, a wife sees another man— a cripple who crawls on his haunches— and takes her pleasure with him.
The wife of King Baka of Bāvarī, who was excessively devoted to sensual pleasures,
did not behave properly toward her husband, who followed the ways of the world.
Nor would any woman ever transgress against another man.
Piṅgiyānī was the beloved wife of King Brahmadatta, the sovereign of the entire world.
She did not act in accordance with the one who followed her heart's desire; though she was full of longing, she did not find him.
Thus ends the first Jātaka, the Kaṇḍarīya Jātaka.
